NVIDIA faces risks related to Chinese government actions, including restrictions on the import and sale of certain automotive products in the United States, which could impact its ability to develop and supply solutions for automotive customers. Additionally, restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on the duration of gaming activities and access to games may adversely affect its Gaming revenue. Increased oversight of digital platform companies may also adversely affect its Data Center revenue. The Chinese government may encourage customers to purchase from China-based competitors, or impose restrictions on the sale to certain customers of its products, or any products containing components made by its suppliers. For example, the Chinese government announced restrictions relating to certain sales of products containing certain products made by Micron, a supplier of NVIDIA. Furthermore, an agency of the Chinese government announced an Action Plan that endorses new standards regarding the compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth of accelerators used in new and renovated data centers in China. If the Chinese government modifies or implements the Action Plan in a way that effectively prevents NVIDIA from being able to design products to meet the new standard, this may restrict the ability of customers to use some of NVIDIA’s data center products and may have a material and adverse impact on its business, operating results, and financial condition.
